name: Reichard's Seedeater
rangeDescription: Southeastern democratic republic of the congo to zambia, tanzania, malawi, and northern mozambique
description: Medium-sized brown seedeater. Note the boldly marked face with a streaked crown, white eyebrow, and broad dark brown patch through the eye; also note pale streaks on breast.

name: Spectacled Finch
rangeDescription: Himalayas (kashmir to nepal and sikkim)
description: Bizarre and unique-looking finch. Note the lumpy diagnostic patch of bright color around the eye and forehead: red in males, yellow in females.

name: Brown-chested Barbet
rangeDescription: Brazil south of the amazon between lower rio madeira and rio tapajós
description: Medium-sized, chunky species with a strong thick bill. Has yellow-olive, cinnamon, and black plumage, duller in females, which also have a black-spotted throat.

name: Mauritius Kestrel
rangeDescription: Dense forest of southwestern mauritius (western indian ocean)
description: Typical kestrel with a rufous back, white underparts, a barred tail, and a dark “moustache” mark on the face. Endangered and endemic to the island of Mauritius.

name: Seram Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Mountains of seram (southern moluccas)
description: A drab brown sparrow-sized songbird with a downcurved bill. Note the pale base to the bill, the thin pale line between bill and eye, the pale skin behind the eye, and the prominent dark streaks on the breast.

name: White-winged Tapaculo
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northern peru (amazonas, south of the río marañón, to huánuco, north of the río huallaga)
description: Described to science in 2020, this tapaculo was long overlooked due to its similarity with other species. It ranges in high elevation cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru.

name: Creamy-rumped Miner
rangeDescription: Andes of central chile and adjacent western argentina
description: Local in the high Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina. Favors open slopes with sandy and gravelly soil, scattered bunch grass and low shrubs, adjacent bogs, and rocky areas.

name: Abbott's Booby
rangeDescription: Christmas island (eastern indian ocean)
description: Gangly, stretched-out-looking black-and-white seabird. Strikingly slender and strange-looking in flight.

name: Scaly-sided Merganser
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern siberia, korean peninsula, and northeastern china; winters to southern china
description: Sleek, secretive diving duck with a bright orange-red bill and a long, shaggy crest. Relatively rare East Asian endemic.

name: Lazuli Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Southern moluccas (ambon, seram, and haruku)
description: A stunning blue-and-white kingfisher with entirely blue upperparts in both sexes. Female has white throat and pale blue breast and belly, but male shows more white, with pale blue confined to belly.

name: Malayan Partridge
rangeDescription: Mountains of malay peninsula
description: Small and reclusive gamebird of the Malay Peninsula’s forested highlands. If seen well, note white cheeks, dark head, and dappled tortoiseshell back and wings.

name: Meyer's Friarbird
rangeDescription: Lowlands of new guinea (except for bird's head peninsula)
description: A drab, uniform brown honeyeater with a long, sharp downcurved bill that lacks any knobs. Juveniles show scaled upperparts and a yellowish throat.

name: Banda Sea Monarch
rangeDescription: Eastern lesser sundas (babar, damar, larat, yamdena, and selaru)
description: A gray-and-white flycatcher-like songbird confined to the eastern Lesser Sundas. Head slate-gray with well-defined black mask and throat.

name: Serra do Mar Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of southeastern brazil (espírito santo to northern rio grande do sul)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long slender tail. Differs from other tyrannulets in being mostly bright olive-green above and gray below with darkish ear patches, prominent white eyerings, and pinkish (not dark) legs.

name: Invisible Rail
rangeDescription: Halmahera (northern moluccas)
description: A huge, distinctive all-dark flightless forest rail with a powerful red bill and red legs. Restricted to the island of Halmahera in the North Moluccas, where it occurs in swampy areas within forest, especially sago swamps.

name: Eyebrowed Jungle Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo (mount kinabalu and adjacent mountains)
description: Distinctive brownish flycatcher found in Borneo’s central and southeastern highland forests. Brown above and gray below, with a warm coffee-brown face and eye-catching white eyebrows and throat patch.

name: Eastern Phoebe
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern canada and usa; winters to southeastern mexico
description: A drab, medium-sized flycatcher. Brownish above and pale below, often with a light yellowish wash on the belly.

name: South Island Saddleback
rangeDescription: Formerly widespread on south island (new zealand); by 1950s confined to south cape islands, now introduced to additional outlying islands
description: A medium-sized songbird endemic to New Zealand, confined to predator-free offshore islands and South Island mainland sanctuaries. Glossy black plumage with distinct chestnut saddle across the back, which gives the bird its name.

name: Yungas Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru (eastern puno) and bolivia (la paz to cochabamba)
description: Small flycatcher found along the east slope of the Andes in western Bolivia, barely reaching over the border into southern Peru. Note the stubby bill, indistinct wingbars, and white eyebrow bordered below by a dark eye-line.

name: Junin Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (junín)
description: Poorly known Peruvian endemic found only in high Andean cloud forest northeast of the city of Huancayo. It was described to science in 2013.
